findings.title: Formula protection misses subscripted variables and removes their grouping
findings.problem: FORMULA and MATH_SIGN recognize unspaced algebraic subtraction only through ASCII-digit patterns. Unicode-subscripted variables bypass those guards, allowing asides() to replace mathematical parentheses with commas. Pure-letter expressions such as HR (EDV-ESV) have the same problem.
findings.failure_scenario: speakable("Oxygen use is CO (CaO₂-CvO₂).") returns "Oxygen use is CO, CaO₂-CvO₂." The parentheses expressing multiplication by the oxygen-content difference have been replaced with a prose pause. This is the subscripted version of an existing test case, but that test uses ASCII digits. The audio gate compares against the already-altered script, so it cannot catch this change to the clinical formula.
findings.fix: Preserve parentheses whenever a group could be algebraic, including Unicode-subscripted variables and pure-letter subtraction. Leave ambiguous groups untouched rather than classifying them as prose. Add exact-output regressions for both CO (CaO₂-CvO₂) and HR (EDV-ESV).

assessment: Request changes: the new aside conversion can remove mathematical grouping from clinical formulas. One blocking defect found.
